solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book to go on coaches — one's ignored deals

indicators.note: the book goes on, that is after, the coaches word
one is ignored, so the letter standing for one is left out of the coaches word

parts.note: coaches are railway carriages, which make up trains
the Roman numeral for one is I
Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone books a coach trip while a lone traveller is overlooked in the arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as 'one is', so 'one's ignored' takes I out of TRAINS, leaving TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, so someone who transacts is making deals.

clue.text: A market set up outside university — it's shocking

indicators.note: outside means the reversed letters go round the university letter
set up, in a down clue, means raised so the words read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A market stall set up beside a university proves a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing experience, something that shocks.

clue.text: Basic actor in difficulty with dramatic movements

indicators.note: in difficulty, in trouble, signals that the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A struggling actor resorts to theatrical gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic tumbling and balancing feats are spectacular, showy movements.

clue.text: Artist gets covered in an amount of mixed chemicals

indicators.note: gets covered in means the artist's name is wrapped inside the amount word

parts.note: some is an indefinite amount
Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist artist

explanation.surface: A painter ends up smeared in a quantity of chemical mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a granular mix of caustic soda and quicklime used to absorb carbon dioxide.

clue.text: Said to pick items from Pick 'n' Mix?

indicators.note: said signals that the word is only heard, and the entry sounds the same

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: A question about selecting sweets from a pick-and-mix counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Pick 'n' Mix is the British self-service sweet counter where you scoop loose sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Chews are soft chewy sweets, the sort found loose in such a counter.

clue.text: Refuse to give up way and go on hunger strike?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to fast is to go without food, as hunger strikers do

explanation.surface: A protester refuses to budge and stops eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give up way' reads as the idiom give way, but the definition stops at 'give up'; 'way' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand firm is to keep one's position resolutely and not yield.

clue.text: Vehicle left outside gym — a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: outside means the vehicle and left letters sit round the gym letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
PE, physical education, is gym at school

explanation.surface: A car parked outside the gym, a minor blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the female reproductive part of a flower, so a piece of a plant in bloom.

clue.text: Brood no end? That's fine

indicators.note: no end means the last letter is cut from the brooding word

parts.note: to brood is to think long and hard

explanation.surface: Endless worrying is acceptable, someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine thread or a fine line is slender, a sense shared with slim.

clue.text: New cadet, due to be this?

definitions.text: New cadet, due to be this?

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh recruit is due to receive training.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is trained and schooled, which leaves him taught and well informed.

clue.text: Sculpture etc. around building is vandalised

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for sculpture and the like is read backwards

parts.note: sculpture, painting and so on are art
a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: A public sculpture surrounded by buildings has been defaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is informal for wrecked or damaged on purpose, as vandals do.

clue.text: Something highway architect might be asked to design in contract

definitions.text: Something highway architect might be asked to design
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a bridge, a structure carrying a road over an obstacle
to shorten, as a text is cut down

explanation.surface: A road engineer is commissioned under contract to design something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a legal agreement in the surface but is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to shorten or condense it, which is contracting it.

clue.text: The old man meeting the devil, said to bring terror

indicators.note: said signals that the letters built are only heard, and the entry is a word sounding the same

parts.words: The old man meeting the devil
parts.note: the old man is PA, a father, and the devil is Old Nick, so PA meeting NICK

explanation.surface: An old man coming face to face with the devil would be frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a synonym of terror.

clue.text: Crowd terribly idle is about to be sent on march?

definitions.text: about to be sent on march?

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: terribly, as in badly done, signals that these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An idle crowd is about to be made to march off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like the reversal or containment signal, but it belongs to the definition: troops mobilised are made ready and so about to march.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobilised troops are called up and prepared for active service, on the point of moving out.

clue.text: Nut to leave boy sated, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is only spoken, and the entry sounds like it

parts.note: to leave a boy sated is to fill him up; Bert is a boy's name, so fill Bert

explanation.surface: A puzzle about feeding a lad nuts until he is full.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is a hazelnut, especially the cultivated kind.

clue.text: Old writer, expert the French regarded as not worth keeping on

parts.note: ex means former, old
a pen is a writing implement
a dab hand is an expert, so dab means expert
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A veteran writer considered by the French as dispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author but is the pen. 'regarded as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dispensable can be sacrificed because it is not worth retaining.

clue.text: Gang showing purpose, about to capture a female

indicators.note: capture means the reversed purpose word holds the next letters inside it
about, turned around, means the purpose word is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: A gang shows its intent by seizing a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is an organised criminal gang, originally Sicilian.

clue.text: Agreeing with action on the parade ground

definitions.meaning: going along with a plan, as in to fall in with it
soldiers taking their places in ranks on command

explanation.definitionFit: To fall in is both to concur with someone and, in drill, to form up in line.

clue.text: Good for Scots to have English adviser?

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good

explanation.surface: A Scotsman would welcome an English adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide shows the way and gives counsel, so is a kind of adviser.

clue.text: Pledge of bloke to suppress an outburst

indicators.note: suppress, hold down, means the bloke word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a guy is a bloke
an indefinite article, A
a rant is an angry outburst

explanation.surface: A man promises to hold back a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A guaranty is a formal undertaking or security, a pledge.

clue.text: Detectives holding up character with bow and arrows?

indicators.note: holding means the detectives' letters keep the next word inside them

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Detectives hold up an armed archer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is pictured as a winged boy with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Carpet material maybe getting female unwell in church

indicators.note: in means the female and unwell letters go inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hen is a female bird
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A woman feels ill in church, perhaps on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tufted velvety yarn or fabric, used for carpets among other things.

clue.text: Fastener caught wedged in piece of wood

indicators.note: wedged in means the caught letter is forced inside the wood word

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fastener got stuck in a wooden board.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a bar or catch that keeps a door or gate shut.

clue.text: Hearing about good person from the south

indicators.note: about means the hearing word goes round the good person's letters

parts.note: aural means relating to hearing
a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A tribunal hearing about a virtuous southerner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a noun but stands for the adjective aural.
explanation.definitionFit: Austral means southern, as in the aurora australis seen in southern skies.

clue.text: Bet agent will appear before second match?

indicators.note: places the agent word ahead of the bet word

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's agent turns up ahead of a rematch.
explanation.definitionFit: When a drawn game is played again, the rerun is a second match.

clue.text: Gradually introduce calm briefly, supporting home

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, puts the calm word under the home word

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: briefly means the calm word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: still means calm

explanation.surface: Advice on bringing calm into the home bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil a habit or idea is to implant it slowly over time.

clue.text: Big beast in union, a dog barking

indicators.note: barking, as in barking mad, signals that these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A large creature and a barking dog together in union.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a large plant-eating dinosaur, certainly a big beast.

clue.text: Employer outside hospital who shows people right place?

indicators.note: outside means the employer word goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: one who employs something, uses it, is a user

explanation.surface: A boss waits outside a hospital to direct people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss, but means one who employs, that is uses, something.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre or church an usher guides people to their seats.

clue.text: Notice written by Irish politicians gets to make sense

indicators.note: written by places the notice word beside, ahead of, the politicians' letters

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A notice drafted by Northern Irish politicians finally makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the DUP sits in Northern Ireland, so 'Irish' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts add up they fit together and are coherent.

clue.text: Women entitled to dismiss English mothers

indicators.note: dismiss means the English letter is sent away from the titled women

parts.note: a Dame is a woman holding a title, the female equivalent of a knighthood

explanation.surface: Titled women are allowed to sack English mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' reads as permitted but means holding a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Dam is the term for an animal's mother, as in horse breeding.

clue.text: Stop to take in every second of big blue fish

indicators.note: take in means the stop word holds the picked letters inside it

parts.note: to halt is to stop

indicators.note: every second letter of the following words is taken, the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A command to halt and admire a big blue fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every second of' picks I and B from BIG and U from BLUE, giving IBU.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: Tiny fellow, almost 11, making contribution to orchestra

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the small crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: almost means the word from the cross-reference loses its last letter

parts.note: the answer to 11 across

explanation.surface: A small man, nearly eleven years old, plays in an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like an age but points to the answer at 11 across, PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are the percussion section's contribution to an orchestra.

clue.text: Transmitter never working at front of room

indicators.note: at front of places the rearranged letters ahead of the room word
working, as in worked into a new shape, signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A radio transmitter never works at the front of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron transmits signals in the nervous system, so it is a biological transmitter.
